LLM_description:
Situation:
Ongoing operations across the Grey Ridge–Koraz Valley corridor have dispersed combat and support elements beyond routine resupply reach. Maneuver units at Forward Operating Base Alpha, Combat Outpost Viper, and Fire Base Orion are drawing heavily on a single critical class of supply. Supply Depot Bravo (western railhead), Depot Delta (forward transshipment), and other depots are operating under throughput and stock constraints while facing intermittent interdiction along Main Supply Route Falcon and Alternate Supply Route Kestrel. Choke points at the river bridges and the Redwood urban corridor require engineer support and route clearance. Weather and terrain further limit movement windows. The threat regularly emplaces IEDs and ambushes along the valley floor and overwatch routes.

Mission:
Deliver required quantities of the designated supply class to supported units throughout the current operational period while minimizing total operational cost, comprising transport costs, shortage penalties, vehicle deployment costs, and fixed route security risk costs.

Execution/Concept:
- Distribution will be planned from multiple depots to supported units over successive days. Flows from each depot are limited by available stocks and handling capacity. Deliveries may be partially deferred, recorded as controlled slack, and penalized accordingly.
- Convoys will be configured to respect vehicle payload capacity by supply volume. Fleet availability is finite and will be managed at the theater level to prevent over-commitment.
- Routes will be activated only when necessary. Critically, activating any route—sending any vehicles at all—incurs a fixed Risk Cost that represents security overhead (escort teams, route clearance elements, overwatch, and comms) regardless of the number of vehicles subsequently dispatched on that route.
- Vehicles can only move on routes that have been activated for the period; route activation decisions will be consolidated to reduce repeated overhead while avoiding risk stacking on exposed corridors.
- Priorities: sustain engaged maneuver units first; maintain minimum medical and water thresholds; consolidate loads to reduce the number of route activations; employ the lower-risk route mix when transport and risk costs outweigh direct movement; accept controlled slack only where tactical risk is tolerable.
- Movement Control Team deconflicts convoy timings with engineer route clearance and QRF coverage. Distribution Management Center monitors depot draws, adjusts flows, and retasks vehicles as conditions change. Units report consumption and receipt to update demand and slack status.
- Constraints:
  • Depot capacity: outbound flows from each depot do not exceed available supply stocks.
  • Demand satisfaction: inbound flows to each unit plus slack meet or exceed stated requirements.
  • Vehicle capacity: loaded volumes per convoy do not exceed vehicle payload capacity.
  • Route activation: vehicles are assigned only to routes that have been activated, incurring the fixed Risk Cost once per route activation per period, irrespective of the number of vehicles.
  • Fleet size: total vehicles employed remain within the available fleet.

LLM_description_template:
Situation:
The division is conducting operations across a dispersed area of operations with multiple forward units maneuvering on separate axes. Ground lines of communication (GLOCs) are contested by indirect fire, improvised explosive devices, and intermittent interdiction at key chokepoints. Weather and terrain restrict movement windows on mountain corridors; urban routes are congested and subject to curfews and civilian interference. Aviation lift is prioritized elsewhere; surface convoys remain the primary means of resupply. Supply Depot Alpha, Supply Depot Bravo, and other intermediate staging bases hold the priority class of supply and are prepared to push forward under movement control.

Mission:
Theater Sustainment Command delivers the designated supply class from available depots to supported units within the planning window, minimizing total operational cost. The cost function includes:
- Transport costs along each depot-to-unit route.
- Vehicle deployment costs per dispatched vehicle.
- Fixed security Risk Costs incurred each time a route is activated (escorts, route clearance, overwatch), regardless of the number of vehicles on that route.
- Penalty costs for any authorized shortfall where demands are not fully met.

Execution/Concept:
- Depot throughput and availability: Each depot’s outbound flow is limited by its on-hand stocks and daily release capacity. Flows cannot exceed depot supply for the period.
- Demand satisfaction with penalties: Each supported unit has a defined requirement. Shortfalls are permitted only as a last resort and will be captured as penalty costs to reflect operational impact.
- Vehicle capacity and conversion: The volume of supply moved determines the vehicles required. Vehicle payload constraints govern how much can be delivered per route; supply volume factors determine conversion from flow to vehicles.
- Route activation and fixed security overhead: A route must be activated before any vehicles can move on it. Activating a route triggers a fixed Risk Cost for that day, reflecting escorts, route clearance, and security overwatch, and this cost applies once per activated route regardless of convoy size. This creates a trade-off between consolidating loads on fewer routes to minimize fixed overhead and distributing loads to meet capacity and risk constraints.
- Fleet limitation: The total number of vehicles dispatched across all routes on a given day cannot exceed the available fleet. Movement Control will prioritize secure corridors and concentrate combat power on fewer, safer routes where feasible, subject to unit timelines.
- Operational risk and constraints: Valley corridors are exposed to observation and indirect fire; movement on these routes requires EOD support, electronic countermeasures, and UAV overwatch. Mountain passes are weather-limited and weight-restricted. Urban corridors require coordination with civil authorities and may close without notice. Engineers and security forces will be allocated only to routes selected for activation.

Command and Signal:
The Movement Control Center will propose the set of routes to activate and allocate vehicles by route and day, balancing risk exposure against transport efficiency and unit priority. Depot chiefs confirm release rates; supported unit S4s validate final receipt windows. The plan seeks to meet critical demands first while minimizing overall costs from transport, vehicle usage, fixed risk overhead, and any unavoidable shortfalls.
